messages.text: What is non-signaling tester, and which product-related measurement decisions depend on understanding it?

The knowledge base gave no validated final answer. It did return partial Raw-cited evidence, summarized below.

A **non-signaling tester** is a production-oriented RF tester used to measure a device’s RF performance **without establishing a full protocol/signaling connection** like a real network or access point would. In the R&S context, the evidence says WLAN production RF measurements are often done in **non-signaling mode to save time**, and Rohde & Schwarz positions the **R&S CMP180** as optimized for that purpose. [7]

In contrast, a **signaling tester** emulates network/AP behavior and is used when the device must be tested under protocol, connection, traffic, interworking, or end-to-end conditions. R&S positions the **CMX500** for R&D signaling and interworking testing, while the **CMP180** is positioned for production non-signaling RF testing. [8] Raw evidence also calls the CMX500 a “5G one-box signaling tester” [65] and a “multi-technology multi-channel signaling tester” for Wi‑Fi 8 signaling test setups. [66]

Product-related measurement decisions that depend on understanding this distinction include:

| Decision | Why it depends on signaling vs. non-signaling |
|---|---|
| **Choose CMX500 or CMP180** | If you need R&D signaling, realistic connection behavior, MLO, coexistence, interworking, or end-to-end testing, the evidence points to **CMX500**. If you need fast production RF measurements, it points to **CMP180**. [6][7][8] |
| **Decide whether protocol/interworking is required** | CMX500 supports 5G/WLAN traffic offloading, N3IWF gateway, Voice over WLAN, and POLQA voice quality measurement, which are signaling/interworking-style needs. [10] |
| **Select product options** | CMX500 options include WLAN signaling options such as 802.11a/b/g/n/ac, 802.11ax, 802.11be, 802.11bn, AP/station testing, 2x2 MIMO, and encryption/authentication. CMP180 options focus on WLAN measurement modes such as SISO, true MIMO 2x2/4x4/5x5/6x6, and PER acknowledgement measurements. [53][54][18] |
| **Plan production RF capacity, bandwidth, and frequency range** | CMP180 supports Wi‑Fi 6E, Wi‑Fi 7, and 5G NR FR1 up to 8 GHz, with bandwidths up to 500 MHz; ordering options include extended 6–8 GHz range and 500 MHz bandwidth. [7][44] |
| **Decide MIMO production scaling** | CMP180 integrates two analyzers, two generators, and two sets of eight RF ports for 2x2 MIMO in one box; two CMP180 units can be combined for 4x4 MIMO AP testing. [7] |
| **Decide whether a non-signaling/GPRF workflow is enough** | CMX500 material also lists non-signaling verification and GPRF generator/standalone TX measurement use cases, so some tasks may not require a full signaling workflow even on CMX500. [28][63] |
| **Test future or wide WLAN waveform candidates** | CMP180 is shown validating a 480 MHz WLAN waveform in loopback mode, described as a potential Wi‑Fi 8 / IEEE 802.11bn candidate rather than a formal Wi‑Fi 8 spec. [7] |

Bottom line: understanding “non-signaling” affects whether you buy/configure/use a tester for **fast RF production measurements**—typically CMP180—or for **protocol-rich R&D, signaling, interworking, and real-world connection behavior**—typically CMX500, based on the cited R&S evidence.

data.answer:
已查到可引用的部分資料：

A non-signaling tester is a production-oriented RF measurement tester used when WLAN device production RF measurements are performed in non-signaling mode to save time; Rohde & Schwarz positions the R&S CMP180 as optimized for that purpose.[7]
Rohde & Schwarz’s product split is that the R&S CMX500 covers R&D signaling and interworking testing, while the R&S CMP180 covers production non-signaling RF testing.[8] Raw Rohde & Schwarz evidence also calls the CMX500 a “5G one-box signaling tester”[65] and a “multi-technology multi-channel signaling tester” with Wi‑Fi 8 testing capabilities in an MWC 2026 setup.[66]
| Product-related measurement decision | Why the signaling/non-signaling distinction matters | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Choose R&S CMX500 or R&S CMP180 for Wi‑Fi work | CMX500 is used for R&D signaling tests under real-world conditions, including RF TX/RX characteristics, MLO, multiple RF chains, 2x2 MIMO, 6 GHz out-of-band discovery, coexistence and E2E test capabilities; CMP180 is used for production non-signaling RF measurements.[6][7] | [6][7][8] |
| Decide whether the task needs protocol/interworking features | CMX500 is used for 5G/WLAN traffic offloading and interworking, with a newly integrated N3IWF gateway for WLAN offloading with Voice over WLAN and integrated POLQA voice quality measurement for early-stage quality-of-experience evaluation.[10] | [10] |
| Select CMX500 signaling options versus CMP180 measurement options | CMX500 WLAN signaling options include 802.11a/b/g/n/ac, 802.11ax, 802.11be, 802.11bn, AP testing, station testing, 2x2 MIMO and advanced encryption/authentication; CMP180 measurement options include WLAN 802.11a/b/g/n/ac SISO, 802.11ax SISO, 802.11be SISO, WLAN true MIMO 2x2/4x4, WLAN true MIMO 5x5/6x6 and WLAN PER acknowledgement measurements.[53][54][18] | [53][54][18] |
| Decide production RF capacity, bandwidth and frequency needs | CMP180 supports Wi‑Fi 6E, Wi‑Fi 7 and 5G NR FR1 up to 8 GHz with bandwidths up to 500 MHz; its ordering information includes R&S CMP-K168 extended frequency range from 6 GHz to 8 GHz and R&S CMP-K185 500 MHz bandwidth.[7][44] | [7][44] |
| Decide whether to measure future/wider WLAN waveform candidates in production-style loopback | CMP180 is shown validating a 480 MHz WLAN waveform in loopback mode, described only as a potential candidate for yet-to-be-defined Wi‑Fi 8 / IEEE 802.11bn and not a formal Wi‑Fi 8 specification.[7] | [7] |
| Decide MIMO production scaling | CMP180 integrates two analyzers, two generators and two sets of eight RF ports for 2x2 MIMO testing in one box, and two CMP180 instruments can be combined for four analyzers and generators for 4x4 MIMO access point testing.[7] | [7] |
| Decide whether a CMX500 non-signaling/GPRF workflow is enough instead of a full signaling workflow | CMX500 callbox material lists non-signaling verification as a use case and describes GPRF generator signal types including ARB, CW, dual tone and replay `.wv` files, plus standalone TX measurements for LTE and NR FR1.[28][63] | [28][63] |
【推論】The practical decision is not simply “which tester is better,” but whether the measurement needs a signaling/interworking environment, which points to CMX500, or fast production RF measurements in non-signaling mode, which points to CMP180.[6][7][8]
